## Natural history notes

A small flower fly characterized by its slender body, large reddish eyes, and yellow-and-black patterned abdomen with thin dark lines that give it a “calligrapher” appearance. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, forest edges, parks, and other sunny habitats with abundant flowers and low vegetation. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen, while the larvae are predators of aphids and other small soft-bodied insects, making this species beneficial in gardens and natural habitats.
